ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: Looking from left to right, there are 6 shapes in the image: a small white square, a large gray square, a small gray triangle, a large white triangle, a large white circle, and a small gray circle. There are only two circles: the large white circle and the small gray circle. Reasoning: Wanda said she chose exactly 2 gray, 2 large, and 2 circles. Because there are only two circles in the image, these two circles both must be chosen. After choosing them, there are already 2 circles, 1 large shape, and 1 gray shape. It is still necessary to add 1 large and 1 gray. In order to make up the difference with the fewest shapes, the large gray square can be chosen; it simultaneously adds 1 large shape and 1 gray shape. Thus, a total of 3 shapes are chosen, and there are exactly 2 gray, 2 large, and 2 circles. Two shapes cannot satisfy the conditions, because the two circles must be chosen, and these two circles themselves provide only 1 large and 1 gray. Therefore the minimum is 3.

method.method_draft: First read the image left to right and tabulate each available shape by three attributes: grey/not grey, big/small, and round/not round. The visible shapes are: small white square, big grey square, small grey triangle, big white triangle, big white circle, and small grey circle. From the text, Wanda’s chosen set must contain exactly 2 grey shapes, exactly 2 big shapes, and exactly 2 round shapes, and we need the minimum number of chosen shapes. Since the image shows only two round shapes, the big white circle and the small grey circle, both must be chosen. These two already give 2 round, 1 big, and 1 grey. To reach exactly 2 big and exactly 2 grey with as few extra shapes as possible, choose the big grey square, which adds both one big and one grey at the same time. This gives 3 chosen shapes total. Also, 2 shapes cannot work because the two required round shapes alone do not provide 2 big and 2 grey, so the minimum is 3.
